newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn, soybean options heat up on frost fears.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn, soybean options heat up on frost fears.

text.p: While forecasters debated the likelihood of an early frost in the U.S. Midwest, Chicago Board of Trade players bought options to insulate themselves from the potential killing freeze, traders and analysts said.
Action in the options pit this week suggested November soybean prices could jump to $9.00 a bushel and December corn to $3.80 if an early freeze devestates the crops.
"I don't think there's a lot of frost premium built in there (futures) yet," said NX Analytics analyst Nick DeBrown. Instead, traders "are buying deep out of the money calls."

Weather Express Chief Forecaster Fred Gesser Thursday forecast a 60 to 70 percent chance for a freeze in Iowa Sept 23 or 24. That prediction reversed calls for a lower CBOT opening. November soybeans closed up 9-1/2 cents at $8.14-1/2 a bushel and December corn ended 3-1/4 higher at $3.30.
"What it does is put the market on guard," DeBrown said of the forecast. "It makes the bears skittish. It puts the bulls in a buy-the-break mentality.
After Gesser's forecast was released, options traders were buying $8.50 and $8.75 soybean calls in the November, said William Gallwas, an options trader with Excellent U.S.A. Inc.

"I'm not really seeing too much fast play but a lot of people are starting to talk about (cool temperatures)," Gallwas said, referring to soybean options. "I've seen more activity in the Dec corn calls for sure," he added.
Floor traders said grain companies -- Continental Grain, Central Soya, Cargill Investor Services and Iowa Grain -- were among those buying calls above current market levels and selling puts below.
Refco Inc and Cargill Investor Services each bought 300 December corn calls at $3.50 on Thursday, traders said.
Wednesday, Central Soya reportedly bought 100 November soybean calls at a $9.00 strike price while O'Connor and Co bought 690 November calls at $9.00, traders said.
Continental Grain reportedly sold 1,000 January soybean puts at $7.75 and bought 800 calls at $8.25, traders said.
Traders said Iowa Grain bought 50 December corn calls at a $3.80 strike price.

Tuesday, traders said Louis Dreyfus bought 700 December corn calls at a $4.20 strike price. Smith Barney bought 1,500 March corn calls at $3.80 per bushel and FIMAT bought 2,000 March calls at $3.80, traders said.
DeBrown said uncertainties about this year's crops have made players especially fearful of holding short positions.

"We've got problems with (the crop) already," he said. "No way do you want to be short when they're talking about frost. "It's highly unusual (to see this kind of options trade) and what it's telling you when they're buying it so far out of the money is, they think they're getting it cheap."
